issues.summary: Trusted bearer scopes filter MCP resources, but scoped tokens can bypass the boundary through tools/call and wonderfood.get_resource.
Server chat principal identity is caller-asserted through x-lifeos-principal instead of bound to the authenticated token.
Hosted startup fails closed without bearer auth and local-dev bypass is loopback-only.
Policy returns one exhaustive deny, clarify, review, or execute decision.
Chat local mutations use action-aware writers, but workflow steps and undo still call direct record mutators and bypass reactive commit delivery.
Undo uses explicit undone and undo_failed lifecycle semantics with canonical receipts.
Verifier false-green hole is closed.
Conversation, chat, and reactive stores use locked mutation, but the canonical MCP state still performs unlocked whole-snapshot writes that lose concurrent updates.
Ingress enforces body limits, total deadlines, idle progress deadlines, and header bounds.
Chat replay state survives restart, but request admission is check-then-execute and does not atomically reserve concurrent idempotency keys.
Hidden plan hint no longer drives intent.
Chat send routes ignore client-supplied previous_response_id.
Retrieval has cache, timeout, circuit-breaker, source-budget, and freshness controls.
Notion pull paginates until target or limit.
A supervised worker drains the outbox, but its file lease uses a non-atomic read-overwrite-read sequence and cannot guarantee one cross-process owner.
Review-required proposals persist as awaiting_review.
Canonical writes atomically persist commit events; startup and supervised worker drains provide idempotent at-least-once reactive delivery across failures and restarts.
Release readiness proof exists, but artifact terminology remains risky.
Ajv strict mode and expanded duplicate, invalid-op, and unknown-field mutants fail closed.
Real SQLite writer-boundary coverage now proves canonical user, sync, AI, undo, JSON persistence, idempotency, and transactional rollback.
Shared confidence contracts converge numeric provenance and qualitative policy semantics.
Current deterministic gates largely pass, but the completion audit is not complete and current-tree security, writer, concurrency, native, and live-authority evidence blockers remain.
Device mutation is emulator-bound; provider mutation requires an acknowledgement label but does not cryptographically or structurally bind that label to the actual Notion or Sheets target.
